banner.title: home-assistant
banner.tagline: Runs Home Assistant on a fixed IoT address, signs users in through Authentik, and serves a code-server editor behind SSO.

explainer.title: One pod, two routes, a login at each door

steps.title: Sign in
steps.text: The install-oidc init container unpacks hass-oidc-auth into /config and checks its SHA-256. Users sign in through Authentik; local login stays as the fallback.
steps.scene: a padlock stamped onto a glowing login card

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Home Assistant listens on 8123. hass.${SECRET_DOMAIN} on envoy-external has no ExtAuth gate, so companion apps can finish their own token flows.
steps.scene: a house with a glowing door beside a globe

steps.title: Address
steps.text: Multus gives the pod net1 at 10.40.0.100 with no MAC pin, so IoT devices keep a stable IP across rollouts.
steps.scene: a fixed address pin on a circuit board

steps.title: Gate
steps.text: The code editor on envoy-internal sits behind SecurityPolicy hass-code-auth, so Authentik checks each request before it reaches the editor.
steps.scene: a gate with a keyhole in front of a code window

steps.title: Keep
steps.text: kopiur snapshots the config claim to R2 each day. Readiness checks /manifest.json inside the cluster, so the public route never decides health.
steps.scene: snapshot cards flowing into a cloud bucket
